scenes.name: Funk rock: Chili Peppers, Primus y la Black Rock Coalition
scenes.book: Funk: The Music, the People, and the Rhythm of the One
scenes.author: Rickey Vincent
scenes.desc: A los blancos les era mucho más fácil tocar funk y grabar: Jane’s Addiction debutó con un directo, Primus de Les Claypool (devoto de Larry Graham), los Limbomaniacs con Bootsy y Maceo, Praxis. Los Red Hot Chili Peppers de Anthony Kiedis y Flea, con Freaky Styley producido por Clinton (1985), versionaron a Sly, los Meters y Stevie y llevaron a P-Funk al escenario de los Grammy de 1993; pero los creadores del funk rock, como los P-Funk All Stars, no tenían esa libertad. En Nueva York Living Colour de Vernon Reid no conseguía contrato pese a tener a Mick Jagger de fan, y Reid y Greg Tate fundaron en 1985 la Black Rock Coalition: «El rock and roll es música negra y nosotros somos sus herederos», contra el «rock de orientación apartheid». Abrió paso a Steve Coleman, Me’Shell NdegéOcello, James Blood Ulmer o el Kelvynator de Kelvyn Bell.

podcast.title: Struggles with Sobriety (1988-1992)
podcast.body: Following Hillel Slovak's death in 1988, Anthony Kiedis was working hard to maintain his sobriety after a "drugs and alcohol bender." His efforts to stay away from heroin, coke, and alcohol led him to distance himself from John Frusciante, whose teenage partying lifestyle was at odds with Kiedis's recovery. He continued to face "continuing sobriety struggles" during the band's turmoil in 1992. "Anthony was working hard to be sober after going on a drugs and alcohol bender after Hillel died."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Long Strange Trip of John Frusciante Part 1

podcast.title: Observing the Changing Musical Guard (1991)
podcast.body: In his autobiography, "Scar Tissue," Anthony Kiedis noted that the "Blood Sugar Sex Magik" tour coincided with a major shift in the musical landscape, observing the decline of late 80s pop metal bands and family sitcoms, and a new energy in music, exemplified by Nirvana's "out of this world" songs. "The Blood Sugar Sex Magic Tour seemed to auger a changing of the musical guard."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Amazing Year That Was 1991

podcast.title: Livid Over Saturday Night Live Performance (1992)
podcast.body: Anthony Kiedis was "livid" and believed John Frusciante "sabotaged everything" during the Red Hot Chili Peppers' "Saturday Night Live" performance. He felt betrayed by Frusciante's "dissonant out of tune experiment" during "Under the Bridge," especially given the live television audience. He confronted Frusciante after the show, suspecting heroin use. "I felt like I was getting stabbed in the back and hung up to drive in front of all of America. While this guy was off in a corner in the shadow, playing some dissonant out of tune experiment."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Long Strange Trip of John Frusciante Part 1

podcast.title: Reaching Out to Frusciante for Reunion (1998)
podcast.body: Following Dave Navarro's firing in April 1997, Anthony Kiedis made the initial move to reconnect with John Frusciante, visiting him at a gallery event where Frusciante's paintings were displayed. Recognizing Frusciante's recovery and lack of an instrument, Kiedis personally bought him a '62 Stratocaster to help him restart his musical journey and rejoin the Red Hot Chili Peppers. "Anthony was the first to reach out by going to a gallery event where John was displaying some of his paintings."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Long Strange Trip of John Frusciante Part 1

podcast.title: Creative Process of Contribution
podcast.body: As part of the band's collaborative songwriting, Anthony Kiedis developed his contributions after John Frusciante and Flea had brought their musical "gems" into practice. His method involved going for "a very long drive in my Chevy" to figure out what he could add to the emerging songs. "I better go for a very long drive in my Chevy and figure out something to add to the stew, which is part of our creative process."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: From Broken Record: The Red Hot Chili Peppers Reunite

podcast.title: Developing Melodic Singing Style with Frusciante
podcast.body: Anthony Kiedis's singing approach became "more melodic" after working with John Frusciante, finding more comfort and confidence with the young guitarist's style than he had with Hillel Slovak. He personally coached the 18-year-old Frusciante, whom the band called "Greeney," one-on-one. "Anthony became more comfortable with John's style. Actually, more comfortable than he had been writing and singing with Hillel."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Long Strange Trip of John Frusciante Part 1

podcast.title: Early Life and Exposure to Drugs and Sex (Childhood)
podcast.body: Anthony Kiedis moved to California to live with his father, Blackie Dammit, a bit-part actor and Hollywood drug dealer, at the age of 12. He recounted in his memoir, "Scar Tissue," an incident at age four where his father blew pot smoke in his face on Sunset Strip. By the time he was 12, Kiedis was clubbing with his father, taking quaaludes provided by his father, and even proposed a sexual encounter with one of his father's girlfriends, Kimberly, which his father facilitated. Keith Moon was an adult friend and role model to Kiedis during his pre-teen years. "When I was about four, my dad and I were on one of our outings walking down sunset strip. When he suddenly stopped and gently blew some pot smoke in my face."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Tales of Weird Rock’n’Roll Sex

podcast.title: Impact of John's Declaration
podcast.body: A single statement from John Frusciante, "I was born to be in this band," profoundly impacted Anthony Kiedis. This declaration made Anthony feel that the reunion was a destined outcome and that he "had no choice" but to fully support it, regardless of the potential consequences. "And he said, I was born to be in this band. And I was just, I was like, he is telling the truth. And there's no fucking winner that I'm going to stop that from happening or do anything other than get out of the way and just let it let it flow."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: From Broken Record: The Red Hot Chili Peppers Reunite

podcast.title: Independent Premonition of John's Involvement
podcast.body: Even before Flea mentioned it, Anthony Kiedis had a strong sensation that "it would be really nice if John would get involved" with the band's music again. He initially considered possibilities like John writing or producing, not necessarily a full rejoining. "I just got the sensation like, it would be really nice if John would get involved."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: From Broken Record: The Red Hot Chili Peppers Reunite

podcast.title: Initial Worries about John's Return
podcast.body: Anthony Kiedis confessed to being initially worried about John Frusciante rejoining the Red Hot Chili Peppers. His concern was that any past resentments could potentially impede the band's success. "Anthony was initially worried that past resentments would get in the way of their success."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Mohican Ancestry
podcast.body: Anthony Kiedis of the Red Hot Chili Peppers has stated that there is Mohican heritage somewhere in his family tree. "Anthony Ketus of the Red Hot Chili Peppers says somewhere in his family tree is Mohican heritage."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Indigenous Alternative

podcast.title: Observation of Flea's Discontent
podcast.body: Anthony Kiedis noticed that Flea was not "feeling his best self" in the band's prior incarnation, describing him as not being "on fire" for whatever reason. This observation contributed to Anthony's independent thoughts about John Frusciante's potential return. "I knew that Flea was in a mood in a disposition where he wasn't feeling his, his, his best self in the previous incarnation. For whatever reason, it just like he wasn't, he wasn't on fire."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: From Broken Record: The Red Hot Chili Peppers Reunite

podcast.title: Reconciliation Meeting with John Frusciante
podcast.body: Anthony Kiedis visited John Frusciante at his home to ascertain John's true feelings and intentions regarding a reunion. He sought to determine if John's desire to return stemmed from "love and creation" or lingering "bitterness." Anthony found "a great deal of resolution," concluding that animosity was resolved. "And walking in and sitting on the couch with him and just trying to get a real sense of, you know, is this coming from a place of love and creation? Or does he still have any kind of bitterness towards me or us?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: From Broken Record: The Red Hot Chili Peppers Reunite

podcast.title: Simultaneous Proposal of John's Return
podcast.body: Anthony Kiedis and Flea remarkably approached each other at the same time, independently, to discuss John Frusciante's potential return to the band. Anthony was planning to suggest John's participation, while Flea was preparing to announce that he had already jammed with John and considered his full rejoining. "And basically, we were both saying the exact same thing at the exact same time, which was what do you think about John?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: From Broken Record: The Red Hot Chili Peppers Reunite

podcast.title: Vulnerability and Confidence in Reunion
podcast.body: Anthony Kiedis admitted to feeling a sense of vulnerability about whether "the old magic" with John Frusciante would still be present upon their reunion, questioning if they would merely be "weird guys in a room." However, he ultimately felt more confident than concerned about the outcome, especially once they started playing. "A little bit, it was kind of a vulnerable feeling because like John said, is the old magic still there? Or are we just going to be some weird guys in a room trying to make it happen?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: From Broken Record: The Red Hot Chili Peppers Reunite

xref.title: Early Formation of the Classic Lineup (1988-1989)
xref.body: Following the death of Hillel Slovak and the departure of Jack Irons in June 1988, the band auditioned Dwayne "Blackbird" McKnight, but he didn't work out. John Frusciante joined as guitarist in October 1988, followed by Chad Smith as drummer in December 1988. By early 1989, this new lineup of Frusciante, Smith, Flea, and Anthony Kiedis formed what would become known as the classic Red Hot Chili Peppers configuration, debuting on the album "Mother's Milk." "By the start of 1989, the Chili Peppers had undergone a complete refurbishment. John was the new guitarist and Chad was the new drummer."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Long Strange Trip of John Frusciante Part 1

xref.title: Quitting Red Hot Chili Peppers (1988)
xref.body: Jack Irons, the drummer for the Red Hot Chili Peppers, quit the band following the death of guitarist Hillel Slovak from a heroin overdose in June 1988, stating he "couldn't take it anymore." His departure left Flea and Anthony Kiedis to decide the band's future. "drummer Jack Irons couldn't take it anymore, so he quit, leaving just flea and anthony to do something, or not."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Long Strange Trip of John Frusciante Part 1

xref.title: Early Red Hot Chili Peppers Dynamics and Drug Use (1989-1991)
xref.body: Upon joining the Red Hot Chili Peppers, Frusciante initially bonded closely with Anthony Kiedis, but their relationship became problematic as Kiedis sought sobriety while Frusciante, a teenager, embraced a wild lifestyle of drinking and drugs, believing it was part of being a "Chili Pepper." He also felt immense pressure to fill Hillel Slovak's shoes. Despite his desire to get high, Frusciante's unique, melodic, "sinewy, slinky, slippery" style of playing was pivotal in transforming the band's sound, making Anthony more comfortable than he had been with Slovak, and influencing Flea's bass playing to become more melodic. "John was this teenager who wanted to drink and do drugs and have sex 24-7. He thought this was how you were supposed to be a Chili Pepper, wild and wacky, in his words."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Long Strange Trip of John Frusciante Part 1

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Alt-Rocks Great Bass Players

xref.title: Aversion to Success and Depression (1991-1992)
xref.body: As "Blood Sugar Sex Magik" grew in popularity, John Frusciante became increasingly unhappy with the band's massive commercial success. He yearned for the underground scene, preferring small clubs over arenas, and his personality shifted from "manic, happy-go-lucky fun" to a more serious and depressed state. This created tension with the band, particularly Anthony Kiedis. He found a kindred spirit in Kurt Cobain of Nirvana, who shared his desire for underground credibility, which further fueled his discontent with the Chili Peppers' mainstream success. "He wanted to be in a cool underground band. The success was way too serious for him."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Long Strange Trip of John Frusciante Part 1

xref.body: Anthony Kiedis, in his autobiography "Scar Tissue," identified Warrant as one of the "cheesy pop metal bands" that were "finished" by 1991, signaling a changing of the musical guard. "Cheesy pop metal bands like Warren's and Poison and Skid Row were finished."

xref.title: Eccentric Behavior and Sunday Night Live Incident (1992)
xref.body: During the tour for "Blood Sugar Sex Magik," John Frusciante exhibited increasingly erratic behavior, including bringing his guitar to meals, chain-smoking, and shaving his head on a whim. He broke a significant band rule by bringing his girlfriend on the European leg of the tour. A pivotal moment occurred during the band's "Saturday Night Live" performance when Anthony Kiedis believed Frusciante sabotaged their set, particularly during "Under the Bridge," where his guitar playing was described as "woozy and weird," and he blasted his guitar and vocals dissonantly at the end. Kiedis suspected Frusciante was on heroin during the performance. "John was experimenting the way he would have if we'd been rehearsing the tune. Well, we weren't. We were on TV in front of millions of people."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Long Strange Trip of John Frusciante Part 1

xref.title: Post-Frusciante Guitarists and Internal Struggles (1992-1997)
xref.body: Following John Frusciante's initial departure, the Red Hot Chili Peppers briefly brought in Arik Marshall, who performed with them at Lollapalooza 1992. After Marshall, Jane's Addiction guitarist Dave Navarro was brought in for one album, but his tenure ended unhappily, and he was fired in April 1997. During this period, Anthony Kiedis continued to struggle with sobriety, and Flea was undergoing a messy divorce, adding to the band's stresses. "Dave Navarro was brought in for one album. That's a whole other story that had an unhappy ending."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Long Strange Trip of John Frusciante Part 1

xref.title: Anthony Kiedis's Rehab and Relapses (1994-1997)
xref.body: Kiedis's first serious rehab stint led to five years of sobriety, but he relapsed in January 1994 after a wisdom tooth extraction led to prescription narcotics (Vicodin and Percodan) and a return to cocaine and heroin. This cycle of getting straight and relapsing continued until 1997, including a stay at Exodus Recovery Center in Marina Del Rey, California. "His first serious trip to rehab left him sober for five years, but then there was a relapse in January 1994 when he had a wisdom tooth removed and the dentist put him on narcotics for the pain, which was a really bad idea."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: RocknRoll Rehab

xref.title: Recovery and Rejoining Red Hot Chili Peppers (1996-1998)
xref.body: John Frusciante quit heroin cold turkey in late 1996, after five years of constant use, though he continued using crack for a couple more years. In January 1998, a friend convinced him to seriously enter rehab. He faced a lethal mouth infection requiring all his rotted teeth to be pulled out and replaced with $75,000 worth of implants to prevent sepsis, as well as skin grafts for abscesses on his arms. After rehab worked, Anthony Kiedis reached out to him at a gallery event showcasing his paintings, and Flea personally invited him to rejoin the band. Frusciante, who didn't even own a guitar, was bought a '62 Stratocaster by Kiedis. The band reassembled in Flea's garage in September 1998, where they began jamming, writing, and recording demos, including an early version of "Californication." "John was rusty both physically and mentally. They started jamming and they started writing."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Long Strange Trip of John Frusciante Part 1

xref.title: Anthony Kiedis's "Last Chance" Rehab (1997)
xref.body: A trip to India sparked a spiritual awakening for Anthony Kiedis. Upon returning to Los Angeles in 1997, he checked into a "last chance" rehab place called the Impact Drug and Alcohol Treatment Center in Pasadena for about a month, a facility known for hosting members of Mötley Crüe and Brent Gerowicz of Bad Religion. This visit initially seemed successful. "A trip to India put him in a spiritual place, and when he got back to LA, he checked into a last chance rehab place called the Impact Drug and Alcohol Treatment Center in Pasadena for about a month."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: RocknRoll Rehab

xref.title: Anthony Kiedis's Motorcycle Accident and Painkiller Addiction (1997)
xref.body: Following a severe motorcycle accident, Anthony Kiedis was prescribed Codeine, Percocet, and OxyContin. Due to his developed tolerance to chemicals, these medications were ineffective against the pain of nine months of physical rehabilitation for a shattered arm. On his 35th birthday, November 1, 1997, he checked into a rehab unit called Steps, but this attempt was also unsuccessful. "The pain of nine months of physical rehab for a shattered arm were extremely painful."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: RocknRoll Rehab

xref.title: Band's State in Late 1998
xref.body: When John Frusciante rejoined in late 1998, the band was in a difficult place, with Flea having issues, Anthony Kiedis battling addictions again, and creative blocks amid divorces and new babies. "The band was not in a good place. Fle was having issues. Anthony was battling addictions again. There were divorces and new babies and creative blocks."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Long Strange Trip of John Frusciante Part 2

xref.title: Dave Navarro's Dismissal (Spring 1998)
xref.body: Dave Navarro was fired in the spring of 1998 due to escalating personal and drug-related conflicts, particularly with Anthony Kiedis, who was attempting to get clean while Navarro was heavily using heroin. Navarro frequently arrived late and high for rehearsals, leading to an argumentative meeting where he fell backwards over an amplifier and stormed out. Bassist Flea's health and relationship issues also contributed to the decision to bring back John Frusciante, ultimately leading to Navarro's ousting. "Dave was out."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: You're Fired!

xref.title: Reunion with John Frusciante (1998)
xref.body: After Dave Navarro's firing in April 1997, Anthony Kiedis and Flea initiated contact with a recovering John Frusciante. Kiedis visited Frusciante's art gallery, and Flea personally invited him to rejoin the band, expressing great happiness at the prospect. Kiedis even purchased a '62 Stratocaster for Frusciante, who didn't own a guitar at the time. The reunited classic lineup began jamming, writing, and recording demos in Flea's garage in September 1998, signifying Frusciante's return after a six-year absence. "Anthony was the first to reach out by going to a gallery event where John was displaying some of his paintings."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Long Strange Trip of John Frusciante Part 1

xref.title: Band Hiatus and Confidence Crisis (2007-2019)
xref.body: After the "Stadium Arcadium" tour ended in August 2007, the band agreed to a long rest, with Anthony Kiedis being particularly tired. During John Frusciante's second absence, the band experienced a "crisis of confidence" and felt "lost" in terms of direction and inspiration. "After the long stadium Arcadium tour wrapped up in August 2007, the band agreed to take a nice long rest. Anthony was especially tired and needed the break."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Long Strange Trip of John Frusciante Part 2

xref.title: Third Return to Red Hot Chili Peppers (2019)
xref.body: Sometime in 2019, John Frusciante re-engaged with Anthony Kiedis and Flea, proposing to work together again after becoming re-excited about playing guitar following his electronic music explorations. He started jamming secretly with Flea, and the musical connection was so strong that Flea quickly decided John needed to be back in the band. "After spending all that time working with electronic music, John had become excited about playing the guitar again. Could they possibly work together again?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Long Strange Trip of John Frusciante Part 2

xref.title: Anthony Kiedis as a Drug Buddy
xref.body: Hillel Slovak's struggles with heroin were exacerbated by his becoming drug buddies with Anthony Kiedis, a situation made worse by Kiedis's openness about his struggles while Slovak kept his addiction secret. "It didn't help that he and Anthony Ketus became drug buddies, and it also didn't help that while Anthony was open about his struggles, Hillel kept his secret."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Last Moments of - Part 3

xref.title: Anthony Kiedis's Childhood Exposure to Drugs
xref.body: Anthony Kiedis was sent to live with his father, Blocky, in Los Angeles, who was a bit actor with a side drug operation. By age 12, Anthony knew how to roll joints and grow cannabis, and by 14, he had tried heroin. "By the time he was 12, Anthony knew how to roll the joints and how to grow a finger now so it could be used as a coax boon by 14, Anthony had tried heroin."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: RocknRoll Rehab

xref.title: Anthony Kiedis's Drug-buying Bridge
xref.body: Kiedis has never revealed the exact location of the bridge in Los Angeles where he used to buy drugs, fearing it might become an unusual fan shrine. Detective work suggests it is likely a bridge in MacArthur Park leading into Wilshire Boulevard. "He's never said where that bridge is because he's afraid that it might become some kind of weird fan shrine."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: RocknRoll Rehab

xref.title: Anthony Kiedis's Early Introduction to Sex, Drugs, and Rock and Roll (Childhood)
xref.body: Anthony Kiedis, born in Grand Rapids, Michigan, moved to California at age 12 to live with his father, Blackie Dammit, who was a bit-part actor and drug dealer in Hollywood. Kiedis was exposed to drugs from a young age; at four, his father blew pot smoke in his face. His father's lifestyle involved frequent clubbing on Sunset Strip and bringing various women home. By age 12, Kiedis was accompanying his father to clubs, using quaaludes given by his father, and even propositioning one of his father's girlfriends, Kimberly, with his father's consent, leading to a sexual encounter while his father watched TV. Keith Moon was also an adult friend and role model to Kiedis during this period. "The Chilling Febrero's with Anthony Kedis, who was introduced to the world of sex, drugs and rock and roll fully by the time he was 12."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Tales of Weird Rock’n’Roll Sex

xref.title: Anthony Kiedis's Heroin Addiction
xref.body: Upon the Red Hot Chili Peppers' formation, Anthony Kiedis's drug habit escalated, with heroin becoming his primary addiction, which he smoked, snorted, and injected. He would disappear from recording sessions for days, becoming a full-blown junkie buying drugs from gang members under a bridge in downtown Los Angeles. "Heroine really was his thing, and I'll smoke it, snort it, and ject it whatever it took."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: RocknRoll Rehab

xref.title: Anthony Kiedis's Initial Reunion Concerns
xref.body: Anthony Kiedis was initially apprehensive about John Frusciante rejoining the band, worrying that unresolved past resentments could get in the way of their future success. He felt the need to understand if John's return stemmed from a place of love and creation rather than bitterness. "Anthony was initially worried that past resentments would get in the way of their success."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: From Broken Record: The Red Hot Chili Peppers Reunite

xref.title: Anthony Kiedis's Long-term Sobriety and Health Consequences
xref.body: By the end of the 1990s, Anthony Kiedis had successfully overcome his addictions and has reportedly remained clean since. However, his past intravenous drug use resulted in a case of Hepatitis C. "All that Ivy drug use resulted in a case of hep C, but at least he's still alive."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: RocknRoll Rehab

xref.title: Anthony Kiedis's Pre-Reunion Sensation
xref.body: Anthony Kiedis observed that Flea was not "on fire" or feeling his "best self" in the band's previous incarnation, which led Anthony to independently wonder about John Frusciante's potential involvement again, initially thinking of him writing or producing rather than fully rejoining. This sensation grew despite no communication with John for some time. "I just got the sensation like, it would be really nice if John would get involved."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: From Broken Record: The Red Hot Chili Peppers Reunite

xref.title: Collaborative Songwriting Process
xref.body: The creative process for new material involved a natural flow of ideas among the members. John Frusciante would bring "gems" (ideas, chord progressions, arrangements, vocal melodies) to practice, which would inspire Flea to bring his own contributions. Anthony Kiedis would then go for long drives in his Chevy to generate his parts and add them to the collective "stew." "It's like every time John would bring a gem into practice, you know, flee would feel like, okay, I'll bring a gem."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: From Broken Record: The Red Hot Chili Peppers Reunite

xref.title: Continued Friendship and Support
xref.body: Despite his firing, D.H. Peligro remained friends with the Red Hot Chili Peppers, and Anthony Kiedis played a significant role in helping him achieve sobriety. "Still, everyone remained friends and Kitas was a big part in helping Pellegros get sober."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: In Memoriam of Those Lost in 2022

xref.title: Declaration of Purpose
xref.body: During his meeting with Anthony Kiedis, John Frusciante made a powerful statement about his connection to the band, declaring, "I was born to be in this band." This statement deeply resonated with Anthony, making him believe that the reunion was an inevitable and destined path. "But he said, I was born to be in this band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: From Broken Record: The Red Hot Chili Peppers Reunite

xref.title: Early Formation and Friendship
xref.body: Hillel Slovak met Anthony Kiedis, Flea, and original drummer Jack Irons at Fairfax High School in Los Angeles, and by 1983, they were all playing together, forming the core of the Red Hot Chili Peppers. "He was born in Israel, and eventually ended up going to Fairfax High School in Los Angeles, where he met Anthony Ketus, Flea, and original peppers drummer Jack Irons."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Last Moments of - Part 3

xref.title: Early Friendship and Songwriting
xref.body: Anthony Kiedis and Flea first met at Fairfax High School in Hollywood, California. Their initial interaction involved Flea "giving a nookie" to Kiedis's only friend at the school. Early in their career, before the band's widespread fame, they wrote a song together during a backpacking trip in the high sierra areas, inspired by their fear of bears. A second verse was later added in Kiedis's backyard on Laurel Avenue. "We actually Flea and I wrote a song early on together in our career before we became the illustrious Red Hot."

xref.title: Friendship with the Band and Anthony Kiedis
xref.body: Peligro had been friends with the Red Hot Chili Peppers for years and was in a joke band called "Three Little Butt Heirs" with Anthony Kiedis, making him an easy initial choice as a replacement drummer. "He'd been friends with the bands for years. He'd also been in a joke band with Anthony Kitas called Three Little Butt Heirs. That's how he was an easy choice for a replacement, at least at first."

xref.title: High Guitarist Turnover Rate
xref.body: The band has a notable history of high turnover for its guitarists, with the observation that "Being a guitarist in the Chili Peppers is the equivalent of being an extra in a red shirt on Star Trek." Drummer Chad Smith and the core duo of Flea and Anthony Kiedis are seen as exceptions to this pattern. "If you're in the Red Hot Chili Peppers and your name isn't Flea or Anthry, you are on Boroughed Time."

xref.title: Hillel Slovak's Denial of Addiction Seriousness
xref.body: Despite Anthony Kiedis's attempts to encourage him to seek counseling, Hillel Slovak dismissed the severity of his condition, stating, "I'm fine. I don't need any medical help, he said. I can manage." "Anthony tried again to get Hillel to see counseling, but he didn't think his condition was serious enough."

xref.title: Introduction to Rock Music
xref.body: Flea's perspective on rock changed after he met Anthony Kiedis and Hillel Slovak at school, leading him to listen to the genre with serious intent. xref.title: John Frusciante's Destiny Declaration
xref.body: During a visit to John Frusciante's house to gauge his intentions, Anthony Kiedis felt a significant resolution of past animosity. John then declared, "I was born to be in this band," which deeply convinced Anthony that the reunion was meant to be, regardless of any potential challenges. "And he said, I was born to be in this band."

xref.title: Keith Moon's Friendship with Young Anthony Kiedis (Childhood)
xref.body: Keith Moon was an adult friend and role model to Anthony Kiedis during Kiedis's formative years, when Kiedis was not yet a teenager. This association exposed young Kiedis to a particular lifestyle, with Moon being described as an adult role model for someone so young. "One adult who became friends with Anthony was Keith Moon."

xref.title: Lost Virginity at Age 12 to Father's Girlfriend, With Father's Knowledge and Consent
xref.body: Anthony Kiedis grew up in Hollywood with his father, who went by Blackie, a drug dealer and bit-part actor who had a series of attractive girlfriends. One night at the Rainbow Room club, Kiedis — who was 12 and had been given cocaine by his father — passed Blackie a note explaining that he found his current 18-year-old girlfriend Kimberly attractive and asking whether a sexual encounter could be arranged. Blackie, proud of his son, brokered the arrangement with Kimberly. They went back to the house, the father set them up in a bedroom and went to watch television, and Kimberly proceeded to sleep with the 12-year-old. "If losing your virginity to your dad's girlfriend with dad's blessing at age 12 isn't a weird sex thing, I really don't know what is."

xref.title: Musical Evolution with Frusciante
xref.body: With John Frusciante's arrival, the Red Hot Chili Peppers' sound underwent a significant transformation. Frusciante's "hooky style of songwriting," emphasizing melody over Hillel Slovak's riff-based playing, made Anthony Kiedis more comfortable and confident in his singing, leading to a more melodic vocal approach. Flea's bass playing also evolved, becoming more melodic and less reliant on finger picking, popping, and slapping techniques, influenced by Frusciante. "Then John Frischionte comes in with his hooky style of songwriting. His playing is more about melody."

xref.title: Reconciliation with Anthony Kiedis
xref.body: Anthony Kiedis visited John at his long-time residence to gauge his feelings about rejoining, specifically looking for any lingering bitterness. Anthony reported feeling "a great deal of resolution," indicating that previous animosity and resentment had largely dissipated. "I felt like whatever sort of animosity or resentment or all this stuff had more or less been resolved."

xref.title: Simultaneous Reunion Discussions
xref.body: Anthony Kiedis and Flea both approached each other at the same time, independently, to discuss John Frusciante's potential return, unaware of the other's thoughts. Flea, however, was a step ahead, having already jammed with John by that point. "Basically, we were both saying the exact same thing at the exact same time, which was what do you think about John?"

xref.title: Withdrawal on "Uplift Mofo Party Plan" Tour
xref.body: For the tour supporting "The Uplift Mofo Party Plan," both Hillel Slovak and Anthony Kiedis resolved to abstain from heroin, resulting in prolonged and painful periods of withdrawal for both, with Hillel's symptoms being particularly severe. "When it came to tour behind the uplift Moful Party Plan, both he and Anthony decided to stay away from her and for the duration of the tour."
